meta.title: Ganesh Nimajjanam Hyderabad 2026
meta.verified_on_note: Facts compiled 19 September 2026 from The Hindu, Deccan Chronicle, BGUS announcements, GHMC/Hyderabad Police advisories and Telangana High Court reporting.

key_facts.label: Mass immersion (main day)
key_facts.detail: Anant Chaturdashi. Celebrations run 12 days from installation on Monday, 14 September 2026 — one day longer than the usual 11.

key_facts.label: Idol installation (Sthapana)
key_facts.detail: Vinayaka Chavithi. Tithi began 7:06 AM IST in Hyderabad.

key_facts.label: Household idol immersion days
key_facts.detail: Family custom decides. Household and small-pandal immersions begin well before the main day — small idols were already being immersed at NTR Gardens, Necklace Road, People's Plaza and the IMAX Theatre lane from 16 September.

key_facts.label: Immersion muhurat (Madhyahna)
key_facts.detail: Astrologically computed window, not a police schedule. The procession itself runs through the day. Confirm with your purohit for a family immersion.

key_facts.label: Designated immersion locations
key_facts.detail: Includes Hussain Sagar (Vinayaksagar), Saroornagar Lake, Ameenpur Lake and Kapra Lake, plus about 110 local ponds and specially built artificial ponds.

key_facts.label: Approved Hussain Sagar immersion spots
key_facts.value: NTR Marg, Necklace Road, People's Plaza
key_facts.detail: Cranes, platforms and equipment are installed at these points. Immersion from the Tank Bund road side is NOT permitted.

key_facts.label: Tank Bund road-side immersion
key_facts.detail: GHMC and Hyderabad Police installed warning banners and a roughly 10-foot railing along Tank Bund to stop direct immersion from the road, citing a High Court order and traffic congestion. The ban applies to the Tank Bund side, not to Hussain Sagar as a whole.

key_facts.label: Plaster of Paris (PoP) idols
key_facts.value: Not allowed in Hussain Sagar or natural water bodies
key_facts.detail: PoP idols must go to artificial 'baby ponds' only. Telangana High Court (2021, reiterated 2023) barred direct PoP immersion in Hussain Sagar and other natural water bodies; the Supreme Court allowed a one-time exception for 2021 only, on the state's undertaking to build alternatives. Baby ponds are provided at Necklace Road and Sanjeevaiah Park among other sites.

key_facts.label: Idol height cap
key_facts.detail: Announced by Hyderabad Police to reduce risk from overhead electrical lines, cable and internet wires, bridges, road clearances and crane movement. Organisers moving large idols must coordinate with traffic police and avoid peak hours.

key_facts.label: Main Shobha Yatra route
key_facts.detail: Balapur Ganesh pandal to Chandrayangutta, Falaknuma, Charminar, M.J. Market, Telugu Thalli Junction and Flyover, then Hussain Sagar. Checked for road condition, height restrictions and overhead clearance.

key_facts.label: Security deployment
key_facts.detail: City Police Commissioner V.C. Sajjanar. The entire route is monitored by CCTV connected to the Command Control Centre, with barricades, cranes, boats, swimmers, ambulances and emergency teams at key locations.

key_facts.label: Expected scale
key_facts.value: About 1.5 lakh idols in Greater Hyderabad
key_facts.detail: In 2025, over 2.54 lakh idols were immersed across Greater Hyderabad limits and more than 20,000 on the final day alone, about 10,000 of those in Hussain Sagar. Comparable or larger numbers are expected this year.

key_facts.label: Public transport on 25 September
key_facts.value: Metro until about 1 AM; overnight MMTS
key_facts.detail: Metro Rail services are expected to run until about 1 a.m. Overnight MMTS services connect Nampally, Lakdi-ka-pul, Khairatabad, Sanjeevaiah Park, James Street and Begumpet. Extra buses and goods vehicles are arranged.

key_facts.label: Road works freeze
key_facts.value: No digging, drilling or cable-laying until immersion ends
key_facts.detail: All ongoing road, nala and slab works on main and feeder immersion routes had to be finished before 14–15 September. Loose and hanging electricity, cable and internet wires are being removed along the route.

key_facts.label: Khairatabad Ganesh
key_facts.detail: A towering clay idol in a large pandal, historically exceeding 60 feet. Its immersion at Hussain Sagar is the focal point of the procession. In 2025 the Khairatabad and Balapur idols were both immersed in Hussain Sagar on the final day.

key_facts.label: Balapur Laddu auction
key_facts.value: Annual auction of the sacred prasadam
key_facts.detail: The Balapur Ganesh laddu is auctioned to devotees, often fetching large sums. The Balapur pandal marks the starting point of the 19 km Shobha Yatra.

key_facts.label: Cranes and immersion throughput
key_facts.detail: Cranes handled the final day in 2025 across 20 major lakes and 72 artificial ponds. More platforms and cranes are being added on the NTR Marg side so more idols can be handled simultaneously; authorities want the main operation to finish the same day.

key_facts.label: Recommended idol material
key_facts.detail: Follow Telangana State Pollution Control Board conditions. Clay and eco-friendly idols may use designated lake-side crane points; PoP idols may not enter natural water bodies at all.
